definition.description: With an intact continuous loop band above both knees, take controlled repeated lateral lead steps and trailing-foot follows on a clear level surface while maintaining the declared band tension and stance. Complete the declared count in one direction, then reverse. This excludes no-band side stepping, ankle or foot band placements, diagonal or forward monster walks, lateral lunges, squats, clamshells, testing, and fatigue-to-failure work.

environment.surface: clear level non-slip lateral travel lane
environment.space: room to take declared lateral steps and reverse without collision
environment.changeRule: Changing band placement, tension, direction, step path, stance, surface, dose, tempo, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can enter, exit, and repeat small lateral steps on the assigned surface
can manage the assigned loop band and stop signal
can retain the declared above-knee placement and controlled step-follow cycle without symptom escalation
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, band, surface, balance, communication, or logistics conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, dizziness, balance, or other stop concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal band color/tension, placement, step width, stance depth, dose, recovery, activation outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 68 reassessed after legacy broad placement instructions; the above-knee loop-band lateral lead-step/follow cycle is distinguished from changed placement, direction, base, action, or loading tasks.

anatomy.laterality: bilateral repeated travel with direction reversal
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, activation, or performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate low-dose elastic-resistance lateral travel only when the exact band placement, lane, cycle, and dose fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Band above your knees: lead sideways, follow under control, then reverse after the count.
secondaryCues: keep steps short enough to stay quiet
do not snap the trailing foot in
make tension or step size smaller before forcing volume
stop for pain, balance loss, or a band problem
expectedSensations: light-to-moderate lateral hip and lower-limb effort
unexpectedSensations: pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, pressure concern, knee or foot symptoms, or a band-driven loss of balance
selfChecks: lead step and follow remain separate

observationChecklist: intact band, declared above-knee placement, and clear lane
lead step, controlled trailing follow, tension, and direction count
trunk/pelvis, knee, ankle, foot, balance, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.band_slip_or_tension_loss: stop, refit or replace band, shorten steps, or revalidate
faultCorrections.trunk_pelvis_or_knee_foot_compensation: reduce step size or tension, restore lane and count, rest, or stop
faultCorrections.fatigue_driven_quality_loss: end the dose; do not convert preparation work into an unplanned burn set

doNotUseWhen: band, travel lane, surface, balance, exit, or communication is unsafe
task conflicts with symptoms or restrictions
intended task uses no band, ankle/foot placement, diagonal/forward travel, lunge, squat, clamshell, testing, or forced dose

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved band, safety, symptom, balance, or quality issues.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any task change reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and validation.

requirements.laterality: bilateral repeated travel with direction reversal
requirements.cycleRule: one lead step and controlled trailing-foot follow is one step; record both directions
requirements.rangeRule: small controlled lateral steps with above-knee band placement, no pain, persistent compensation, unsafe balance, or forced tension

dosage.countRule: count only controlled lead-step and trailing-foot-follow cycles while placement, tension, balance, and quality remain controlled

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Band placement, lane, lead step, trailing follow, tension, stance, balance, lower-limb path, and direction count remain controlled with no stop symptom.
stopRules: stop on pain, new symptoms, dizziness, band failure, surface hazard, loss of balance, or participant request
stop when above-knee placement, lead-step/follow cycle, tension, stance, balance, or controlled direction reversal cannot be restored
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Inspect and fit the band, set a short clear lane, observe both directions, shorten step or reduce tension before volume, and revalidate any placement, direction, load, surface, or support change.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Set the band above your knees, lead sideways, follow quietly, keep the band gently tensioned, reverse after the count, and stop for pain, balance loss, or a band problem.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate preparation only; no outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: smaller steps, lower tension, fewer steps, shorter lane, more rest, or another reviewed task
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not move the band to ankles or feet, remove it, change travel direction, add squat/lunge work, raise tension, test, or force dose without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Band above knees; lead, follow, reverse.
supportPrompts.coach: Band placement and travel direction are identity boundaries, not athlete-skill labels.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact above-knee loop band, short lateral lane, lead-step/follow cycle, balance, symptoms, communication, dose, and downstream task—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm band integrity, placement, and safe removal
confirm clear level travel lane and stop signal
confirm small controlled steps in both directions
stopSigns: dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, balance, or other unusual symptoms
band failure, surface hazard, or persistent quality loss
contraindications: no-band, ankle/foot-band, diagonal/forward, lunge, squat, clamshell, testing, or forced-dose intent
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after revalidation.
Do not treat no-band side stepping, ankle/foot placement, Monster Walk, Lateral Lunge, Clamshell, or Banded Squat as automatic substitutions.
